page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. The system features 16 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs running on an AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning includes 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 950 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage and maintains a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced parallel execution across all 16 physical cores, offset by modest single-threaded throughput. The platform recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 8497.0 and a multi-threaded stress-ng metric of 24294.54, contrasting with a single-core Geekbench score of 934.0 and weak single-threaded compression throughput. In data serving and retrieval benchmarks, the instance sustained 19.13 million Redis SET operations per second and 19.25 GB/s in static web serving throughput. Natural language model inference benchmarks demonstrate lower responsiveness, consistent with the absence of discrete GPU accelerators and matrix extensions.

The integration of a direct-attached 950 GB NVMe SSD provides low-latency local scratch and caching capacity without relying exclusively on networked block storage. The Neoverse-N1 architecture offers high compute density per physical core, making the configuration cost-efficient for scale-out parallel architectures. Primary tradeoffs involve lower single-core execution speed and the need to compile software for the arm64 instruction set. Best-fit workloads include multi-threaded compilation pipelines, distributed web serving, caching tiers, microservices, and intermediate data staging.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 16-core AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs, 32.0 GB of system memory, and 950 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, the instance maintains a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio along with a 5 Gbps baseline network profile. Multi-core performance is solid, indicated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8497.0, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 60.25 GB/s, and Redis throughput of 19.13 million SET operations per second. Conversely, single-thread throughput and machine learning inference speeds reflect lower operational tiers. Bundled high-speed local storage minimizes networked disk latency, offering high efficiency for multi-threaded build jobs, distributed web servers, batch processors, and caching clusters.
